solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Writer’s copy replacing contents of schedule (6)

indicators.note: the copy takes the place of the inside letters of the next word, leaving only its outer pair

blocks.note: first letter of SCHEDULE, kept as its contents go
to crib is to copy another's work

annotation.surface: A writer caught lifting someone else's timetable.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', so 'Writer' stands alone as the definition. SCHEDULE keeps only S…E, and CRIB fills the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A scribe is a writer, originally one who copied manuscripts by hand.

entries.clue: Holding up two notes, stiff VIP (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the notes sit above the next piece, supporting it from the top

blocks.note: so(h), fifth note of the sol-fa scale
me (mi), third note of the sol-fa scale
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a body

annotation.surface: Someone propping up a rigid celebrity while humming a couple of notes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective describing the VIP; it is the noun, a dead body.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, as in 'she's a real somebody', it means a person of note, which a VIP is.

entries.clue: Right time to return starter of bruschetta and Italian dish (7)

indicators.note: return = go back, so the time word is written backwards
the starter of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: IT = Italian (as in gin and it, Italian vermouth)

annotation.surface: A restaurant deciding the moment is right to bring back its Italian starter.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian menu is a decoy: the dish is Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast.
annotation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

entries.clue: Raise about a thousand more, without opening shop (9)

indicators.note: the raise word goes round the thousand
the next word loses its first letter

blocks.note: K = a thousand, inserted in BOO…ST

annotation.surface: A fundraiser asking for another thousand, while the shop stays shut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without opening' reads as a shop that is closed; it strips the M from MORE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the store in the compound is the American word for a shop.

entries.clue: First duo in studio vocalised with bands? (8)

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Musicians recording in a studio, singing with their bands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests musical groups; the question mark flags it as straps, so STRAPPED means fitted with bands.
annotation.definitionFit: Something strapped is fastened with straps, which are bands.

entries.clue: Type that finds fault gets up one’s nose? (14)

blocks.note: what gets up your nose troubles you
hooter is British slang for nose

annotation.surface: An irritating fault-finder who annoys everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is re-spacing the answer: the familiar job title hides a two-word sentence. The question mark flags that the wordplay is a playful paraphrase of an idiom for annoying someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is someone whose job is to find and fix faults.

entries.clue: Train drivers cut across middle of sidings to get to walkway (5)

indicators.note: the union's name is cut short, losing its last letter
the shortened name lies across the extra letter, enclosing it
the centre letter of the next word

blocks.note: ASLEF, the British train drivers' union, minus its last letter
middle letter of SIDINGS, placed inside A…SLE

annotation.surface: Train drivers taking a shortcut over the sidings to reach a footpath.
annotation.walkthrough: ASLEF (Associated Society of Locomotive Engineers and Firemen) is the British train drivers' union. 'Cut' looks like drivers crossing; it docks the F.
annotation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats.

entries.clue: Rising very quietly, sailor drinks whiskey following hostilities (4-3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the letters go backwards
the sailor takes the whiskey inside, as one drinks

blocks.note: W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet, inside T…AR

annotation.surface: A sailor quietly getting drunk on whiskey once the fighting is over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very quietly' tempts as PP, the musical marking; here it is SO + P.
annotation.definitionFit: Hostilities is a formal word for fighting, and the adjective describes the period once a war has ended.

entries.clue: Before end of adventure, French couple takes in Lake Superior (6)

indicators.note: the French pair comes ahead of the next piece
the last letter of the word that follows
the couple swallows the lake inside it

annotation.surface: A French pair on holiday visiting Lake Superior before the trip ends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' reads as the Great Lake; the phrase splits, L for lake and 'Superior' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Deluxe means of superior quality, luxurious.

entries.clue: Recycled tyre and used oil for home mechanic, perhaps (2-2-10)

indicators.note: recycled material is broken up and remade, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone who fixes their own car and recycles old tyres and sump oil.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'and' only joins the two stretches of fodder; it contributes no letters. 'Perhaps' marks the home mechanic as one example of a do-it-yourselfer.
annotation.definitionFit: A do-it-yourselfer does their own repairs rather than paying a tradesman, as a home mechanic does.

entries.clue: Retired old hack to finally study Venetian figure (5,4)

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the whole string is written backwards
the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to hack is to lop, chop off
to cram is to study hard

annotation.surface: A retired old journalist settling down to write about a Venetian.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old hack' reads as a veteran journalist; the words split into O and LOP. OLOPOCRAM reversed is MARCOPOLO.
annotation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant famed for his travels to China.

entries.clue: Plant from India collected by girl heading west (5)

indicators.note: the girl gathers the I inside her
in an across clue, going west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: I = India in the NATO alphabet, inside LAS…S

annotation.surface: A girl on her way west carrying a plant she brought back from India.
annotation.walkthrough: LAS(I)S is LASIS, which reversed gives SISAL.
annotation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant grown for its fibre.

entries.clue: Watch over young mammal sheltering by small island (4-3)

indicators.note: the mammal shelters the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: a bat is a mammal; 'young' is part of the surface only
I = island; BY S I goes inside BA…T

annotation.surface: Someone guarding a young animal as it hides beside a little island.
annotation.walkthrough: Unusually, 'by' is not a link: it is itself one of the pieces sheltered inside BAT.
annotation.definitionFit: To baby-sit is to watch over children while their parents are out.

entries.clue: Polish constituent was confused by vote after social gathering (7)

indicators.note: the letters of 'was' are mixed up
the mixed letters and vote come after the gathering

blocks.note: a bee is a gathering for work and company, as in a sewing bee
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

annotation.surface: A Polish voter bewildered by the ballot after a party.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is polish for furniture.
annotation.definitionFit: Beeswax is a key ingredient of furniture polish.

entries.clue: Copper knocked back too much — same again? (5)

indicators.note: knocked backwards, so the letters are reversed

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, a police officer
OTT = over the top, too much, turned round

annotation.surface: A policeman who has downed too much ordering the same again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman, not the metal Cu, and 'knocked back' sounds like drinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to repeat what was said before.

entries.clue: Plain vase is upset (8)

annotation.surface: A plain vase has been knocked over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the vase being knocked over; it is the definition, as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the literal sense of tipping something over, as one upsets a cup.

entries.clue: Wrong turn — other direction (4,5)

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A driver who took a wrong turn and should have gone the other way.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that the anagram of a wrong turn gives the one direction that never changes.
annotation.definitionFit: A compass bearing is a direction, and this one points to the geographic pole rather than the magnetic one.

entries.clue: Crew start to search river for clothing (8)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Wear, a river in north-east England

annotation.surface: A crew beginning to comb a river for clothes someone lost.
annotation.walkthrough: The Wear runs through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England.
annotation.definitionFit: The general word 'clothing' covers this shop-department term for garments made for men.

entries.clue: Look into structural support after end of downpour and see crumbling (8)

indicators.note: the support comes after the other pieces
the last letter of the word that follows
the letters of 'see' break up and rearrange

annotation.surface: A surveyor inspecting a support after a storm and finding it crumbling.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is building survey; ARCH comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to investigate a subject systematically.

entries.clue: Implement buried in garden for centuries (7)

indicators.note: the answer lies buried in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A garden tool that has lain in the soil for hundreds of years.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Implement' reads as a noun, a garden tool; it is the verb, to put into effect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when the object is a law or policy: to put it into effect.

entries.clue: Article removed from grubby pawnbroker (5)

indicators.note: the article is taken out of the next word

blocks.note: AN, the indefinite article, taken from the end of the grubby word

annotation.surface: A dirty-dealing pawnbroker having an item taken away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker. 'Article' looks like a pawned item; it is the grammatical article AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Uncle is an old slang word for a pawnbroker.

entries.clue: Clubs help to hold popular assembly (7)

indicators.note: the help word holds the next piece inside it

annotation.surface: Social clubs pitching in to stage a popular gathering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular assembly' reads as one phrase; it splits into IN and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabinet is the assembly of senior ministers in a government.

entries.clue: Two male animals picked up rodent (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: Two male animals caught a rodent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a homophone signal; in a down clue it lifts TOMRAM to MARMOT.
annotation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large burrowing rodent of the squirrel family.

entries.clue: Good-humoured American, very loud and fit (7)

blocks.note: ff = fortissimo, very loud in music

annotation.surface: A cheerful, loud and healthy American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very loud' is the musical marking ff, fortissimo, and 'fit' means capable rather than healthy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone pleasant and easy to talk to.

entries.clue: Republican leaves meal for group (5)

indicators.note: the Republican departs from the meal word

blocks.note: R = Republican, taken out of B(R)UNCH

annotation.surface: A Republican walking out of a group lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: Brunch is the late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch; 'leaves' is the verb, not foliage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'a bunch of friends'.

entries.clue: Revolutionary throw in wrestling leads to collection of titles (7)

indicators.note: revolving turns the whole thing round, so it is written backwards
the throw word goes inside the wrestling word

blocks.note: to bin is to throw away

annotation.surface: A revolutionary wrestling throw that leads to a string of championship titles.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all sport, with 'titles' as championships; they are book titles. SU(BIN)MO reversed gives OMNIBUS.
annotation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a volume collecting several works, a collection of titles.

entries.clue: Idiot accepted standard returns, saving nothing (5)

indicators.note: the standard comes back, written backwards
it keeps the nothing safe inside it

blocks.note: a norm is an accepted standard; NORM turned round

annotation.surface: A fool who took the standard refund and saved nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like money back; it reverses NORM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are insults for a stupid person, moron once being a clinical term.

entries.clue: Without charge, capacity’s not in battery? (4-5)

annotation.surface: A question about an electrical battery with no charge left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' and 'battery' paint electrics; the definition means hens not kept in battery cages.
annotation.definitionFit: Free-range hens roam outdoors rather than living in battery cages.

entries.clue: Top golf equipment? Second shot goes over back of bunker (3,5)

indicators.note: the shot goes over the letter, enclosing it
the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball is set on
last letter of BUNKER, inside HI…T

annotation.surface: A golfer's second shot clearing the back of a sand bunker.
annotation.walkthrough: Everything suggests golf, but 'Top' is a garment. The question mark admits a tee is only one item of golf equipment.
annotation.definitionFit: A top is any upper-body garment, and this T-shaped cotton one is the commonest.

entries.clue: More milky? Tiny bit about to turn (6)

indicators.note: the about word is turned round

blocks.note: a whit is a tiny bit, as in 'not a whit'

annotation.surface: Milk that is on the verge of turning sour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About to turn' reads as milk going off; it is RE, then the instruction to reverse it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: milk is the standard of whiteness, so 'more milky' describes a paler colour.
